uniforms.name: Ascii_spacing
uniforms.label: Character Spacing
uniforms.tip: Determines the spacing between characters. I feel 1 to 3 looks best.

uniforms.name: Ascii_font_color_mode
uniforms.label: Font Color Mode
uniforms.tip: 0 = Foreground color on background color, 1 = Colorized grayscale, 2 = Full color

uniforms.name: Ascii_swap_colors
uniforms.label: Swap Colors
uniforms.tip: Swaps the font and background color when you are too lazy to edit the settings above (I know I am)

uniforms.name: FogColor
uniforms.label: FogColor
uniforms.tip: Color of the fog, in (red , green, blue)

uniforms.name: MaxFogFactor
uniforms.label: MaxFogFactor
uniforms.tip: The maximum fog factor. 1.0 makes distant objects completely fogged out, a lower factor will shimmer them through the fog.

uniforms.name: FogCurve
uniforms.label: FogCurve
uniforms.tip: The curve how quickly distant objects get fogged. A low value will make the fog appear just slightly. A high value will make the fog kick in rather quickly. The max value in the rage makes it very hard in general to view any objects outside fog.

uniforms.name: FogStart
uniforms.label: FogStart
uniforms.tip: Start of the fog. 0.0 is at the camera, 1.0 is at the horizon, 0.5 is halfway towards the horizon. Before this point no fog will appear.

uniforms.name: BloomThreshold
uniforms.label: BloomThreshold
uniforms.tip: Threshold for what is a bright light (that causes bloom) and what isn't.

uniforms.name: Auto_Bloom
uniforms.label: Auto Bloom
uniforms.tip:
Auto Intensity will enable the shader to adjust Bloom Intensity automaticly though Bloom Opacity above.
Auto Saturation will enable the shader to adjust Bloom Saturation automaticly though Bloom Saturation above.
Default is Off.

uniforms.name: CBT_Adjust
uniforms.label: Extracting Bright Colors
uniforms.tip:
Use this to set the color based brightness threshold for what is and what isn't allowed.
This is the most important setting, use Debug View to adjust this.
Default Number is 0.5.

uniforms.name: Bloom_Intensity
uniforms.label: Bloom Intensity & Bloom Opacity
uniforms.tip:
Use this to set Primary & Secondary Bloom Intensity and Overall Bloom Opacity for your content.
Number 0.1 & 0.5 is default.

uniforms.name: BloomSensitivity
uniforms.label: Bloom Sensitivity
uniforms.tip: A Curve that is applied to the bloom input.

uniforms.name: BloomCurve
uniforms.label: Bloom Curve
uniforms.tip: Defines the way the bloom spreads.

uniforms.name: Saturation
uniforms.label: Bloom Saturation & Auto Cutoff Point
uniforms.tip:
Adjustment The amount to adjust the saturation of the Bloom.
Number 0.25 is default for both.

uniforms.name: Bloom_Spread
uniforms.label: Bloom Spread
uniforms.tip:
Adjust to spread out the primary Bloom.
This is used for spreading Bloom.
Number 1.0 is default.

uniforms.name: Dither_Bloom
uniforms.label: Bloom Dither
uniforms.tip:
Adjustment The amount Dither on bloom to reduce banding.
Number 0.25 is default.

uniforms.name: Tonemappers
uniforms.label: Tonemappers
uniforms.tip: Changes how color get used for the other effects.

uniforms.name: GreyValue
uniforms.label: Exposure 50% Greyvalue
uniforms.tip: Exposure 50% Greyvalue Set this Higher when using ACES Fitted and Lower when using Timoithy.

uniforms.name: Gamma
uniforms.label: Gamma value
uniforms.tip: Most monitors/images use a value of 2.2. Setting this to 1 disables the inital color space conversion from gamma to linear.

uniforms.name: Saturate
uniforms.label: Image Saturation
uniforms.tip:
Adjustment The amount to adjust the saturation of the color in the image.
Number 1.0 is default.

uniforms.name: Inv_Tonemappers
uniforms.label: Extract HDR Information
uniforms.tip:
Changes how color get used for the other effects.
Turn this Off when the game has a good HDR implementation.

uniforms.name: HDR_BP
uniforms.label: HDR Power
uniforms.tip:
Use adjsut the HDR Power, You can override this value and set it to like 1.5 or something.
Number 0.5 is default.

uniforms.name: Bloom_BA_iToneMapper
uniforms.label: HDR Bloom Application
uniforms.tip: This will let you swap between Befor HDR ToneMapper and After.

uniforms.name: Auto_Exposure
uniforms.label: Auto Exposure Type
uniforms.tip:
This will enable the shader to adjust Exposure automaticly.
This will also turn on Eye Adaptation for this shader.
This is based off Prod80's Port of an Auto-Expo Algo.
Padraic Hennessy, MJP and David Neubelt.

uniforms.name: Adapt_Adjust
uniforms.label: Eye Adapt Speed
uniforms.tip:
Use this to Adjust Eye Adaptation Speed.
Set from Zero to One, Zero is the slowest.
Number 0.5 is default.

uniforms.name: Adapt_Seek
uniforms.label: Eye Adapt Seeking
uniforms.tip:
Use this to Adjust Eye Seeking Radius for Average Brightness.
Set from 0 to 1, 1 is Full-Screen Average Brightness.
Number 0.5 is default.

uniforms.name: Debug_View
uniforms.label: Debug View
uniforms.tip: To view Shade & Blur effect on the game, movie piture & ect.

uniforms.name: border_width
uniforms.label: Size
uniforms.tip: Measured in pixels. If this is set to zero then the ratio will be used instead.

uniforms.name: border_ratio
uniforms.label: Size Ratio
uniforms.tip: Set the desired ratio for the visible area.

uniforms.name: Amount
uniforms.label: Amount
uniforms.tip: Amount of CRT effect you want

uniforms.name: Resolution
uniforms.label: Resolution
uniforms.tip: Input size coefficient (low values gives the 'low - res retro look').

uniforms.name: Brightness
uniforms.label: Brightness
uniforms.tip: Used to boost brightness a little.

uniforms.name: ScanlineGaussian
uniforms.label: Scanline Bloom Effect
uniforms.tip: Use the new nongaussian scanlines bloom effect.

uniforms.name: ViewerDistance
uniforms.label: ViewerDistance
uniforms.tip: Simulated distance from viewer to monitor

uniforms.name: Oversample
uniforms.label: Oversample
uniforms.tip: Enable 3x oversampling of the beam profile (warning : performance hit)

uniforms.name: EdgeSlope
uniforms.label: Edge Slope
uniforms.tip: Raise this to filter out fainter edges. You might need to increase the power to compensate. Whole numbers are faster.

uniforms.name: Shift
uniforms.label: Shift
uniforms.tip: Distance (X,Y) in pixels to shift the color components. For a slightly blurred look try fractional values (.5) between two pixels.

techs.name: CinematicDOF
techs.label: CinematicDOF
techs.tip:
Cinematic Depth of Field v1.2.10
===========================================

Cinematic Depth of Field is a state of the art depth of field shader,
offering fine-grained control over focusing, blur aspects and highlights,
using real-life lens aspects. Cinematic Depth of Field is based on
various papers, of which the references are included in the source code.

Cinematic Depth of Field was written by Frans 'Otis_Inf' Bouma and is part of OtisFX
https://fransbouma.com | https://github.com/FransBouma/OtisFX

uniforms.name: UseAutoFocus
uniforms.label: Use auto-focus
uniforms.tip:
If enabled it will make the shader focus on the point specified as 'Auto-focus point',
otherwise it will put the focus plane at the depth specified in 'Manual-focus plane'.

uniforms.name: UseMouseDrivenAutoFocus
uniforms.label: Use mouse-driven auto-focus
uniforms.tip:
Enables mouse driven auto-focus. If enabled, and 'Use auto-focus' is enabled, the
auto-focus point is read from the mouse coordinates, otherwise the 'Auto-focus point' is used.

uniforms.name: AutoFocusPoint
uniforms.label: Auto-focus point
uniforms.tip:
The X and Y coordinates of the auto-focus point. 0,0 is the upper left corner,
and 0.5, 0.5 is at the center of the screen. Only used if 'Use auto focus' is enabled.

uniforms.name: AutoFocusTransitionSpeed
uniforms.label: Auto-focus transition speed
uniforms.tip:
The speed the shader will transition between different focus points when using auto-focus.
0.001 means very slow, 1.0 means instantly. Only used if 'Use auto-focus' is enabled.

uniforms.name: ManualFocusPlane
uniforms.label: Manual-focus plane
uniforms.tip:
The depth of focal plane related to the camera when 'Use auto-focus' is off.
Only used if 'Use auto-focus' is disabled.

uniforms.name: FocalLength
uniforms.label: Focal length (mm)
uniforms.tip:
Focal length of the used lens. The longer the focal length, the narrower the
depth of field and thus the more is out of focus. For portraits, start with 120 or 150.

uniforms.name: FNumber
uniforms.label: Aperture (f-number)
uniforms.tip:
The f-number (also known as f-stop) to use. The higher the number, the wider
the depth of field, meaning the more is in-focus and thus the less is out of focus.
For portraits, start with 2.8.

uniforms.name: ShowOutOfFocusPlaneOnMouseDown
uniforms.label: Show out-of-focus plane overlay on mouse down
uniforms.tip:
Enables the out-of-focus plane overlay when the left mouse button is pressed down,
which helps with fine-tuning the focusing.

uniforms.name: OutOfFocusPlaneColor
uniforms.label: Out-of-focus plane overlay color
uniforms.tip:
Specifies the color of the out-of-focus planes rendered when the left-mouse button
is pressed and 'Show out-of-focus plane on mouse down' is enabled. In (red , green, blue)

uniforms.name: OutOfFocusPlaneColorTransparency
uniforms.label: Out-of-focus plane transparency
uniforms.tip: Amount of transparency of the out-of-focus planes. 0.0 is transparent, 1.0 is opaque.

uniforms.name: FocusPlaneColor
uniforms.label: Focus plane overlay color
uniforms.tip:
Specifies the color of the focus plane rendered when the left-mouse button
is pressed and 'Show out-of-focus plane on mouse down' is enabled. In (red , green, blue)

uniforms.name: FocusCrosshairColor
uniforms.label: Focus crosshair color
uniforms.tip:
Specifies the color of the crosshair for the auto-focus.
Auto-focus must be enabled

uniforms.name: FarPlaneMaxBlur
uniforms.label: Far plane max blur
uniforms.tip:
The maximum blur a pixel can have when it has its maximum CoC in the far plane. Use this as a tweak
to adjust the max far plane blur defined by the lens parameters. Don't use this as your primarily
blur factor, use the lens parameters Focal Length and Aperture for that instead.

uniforms.name: NearPlaneMaxBlur
uniforms.label: Near plane max blur
uniforms.tip:
The maximum blur a pixel can have when it has its maximum CoC in the near Plane. Use this as a tweak to
adjust the max near plane blur defined by the lens parameters.  Don't use this as your primarily blur factor,
use the lens parameters Focal Length and Aperture for that instead.

uniforms.name: BlurQuality
uniforms.label: Overall blur quality
uniforms.tip:
The number of rings to use in the disc-blur algorithm. The more rings the better
the blur results, but also the slower it will get.

uniforms.name: BokehBusyFactor
uniforms.label: Bokeh busy factor
uniforms.tip: The 'bokeh busy factor' for the blur: 0 means no busyness boost, 1.0 means extra busyness boost.

uniforms.name: PostBlurSmoothing
uniforms.label: Post-blur smoothing factor
uniforms.tip: The amount of post-blur smoothing blur to apply. 0.0 means no smoothing blur is applied.

uniforms.name: NearFarDistanceCompensation
uniforms.label: Near-Far plane distance compenation
uniforms.tip:
The amount of compensation is applied for edges which are far away from the background.
Increase to a value > 1.0 to avoid hard edges in areas out of focus which
are close to the in-focus area.

uniforms.name: HighlightAnamorphicFactor
uniforms.label: Anamorphic factor
uniforms.tip:
The anamorphic factor of the bokeh highlights. A value of 1.0 (default) gives perfect
circles, a factor of e.g. 0.1 gives thin ellipses

uniforms.name: HighlightAnamorphicSpreadFactor
uniforms.label: Anamorphic spread factor
uniforms.tip:
The spread factor for the anamorphic factor. 0.0 means it's relative to the distance
to the center of the screen, 1.0 means the factor is applied everywhere evenly,
no matter how far the pixel is to the center of the screen.

uniforms.name: HighlightAnamorphicAlignmentFactor
uniforms.label: Anamorphic alignment factor
uniforms.tip:
The alignment factor for the anamorphic deformation. 0.0 means you get evenly rotated
ellipses around the center of the screen, 1.0 means all bokeh highlights are
aligned vertically.

uniforms.name: HighlightBoost
uniforms.label: Highlight boost factor
uniforms.tip: Will boost/dim the highlights a small amount

uniforms.name: HighlightGammaFactor
uniforms.label: Highlight gamma factor
uniforms.tip:
Controls the gamma factor to boost/dim highlights
2.2, the default, gives natural colors and brightness

uniforms.name: HighlightSharpeningFactor
uniforms.label: Highlight sharpening factor
uniforms.tip: Controls the sharpness of the bokeh highlight edges.

uniforms.name: HighlightShape
uniforms.label: Highlight custom shape
uniforms.tip:
Controls if a custom shape has to be used for the highlights.
Circle means no custom shape.
Anamorphic distortion only works with Circle

uniforms.name: HighlightShapeRotationAngle
uniforms.label: Shape rotation
uniforms.tip: Controls the rotation of the shape

uniforms.name: HighlightShapeGamma
uniforms.label: Shape gamma correction
uniforms.tip:
Controls the gamma of the shape.
Normally this should be 2.20

uniforms.name: MitigateUndersampling
uniforms.label: Mitigate undersampling
uniforms.tip:
If you see bright pixels in the highlights,
check this checkbox to smoothen the highlights.
Only needed with high blur factors and low blur quality.

uniforms.name: ShowCoCValues
uniforms.label: Show CoC values and focus plane
uniforms.tip: Shows blur disc size (CoC) as grey (far plane) and red (near plane) and focus plane as blue

uniforms.name: ClarityRadius
uniforms.label: ClarityRadius
uniforms.tip: [0|1|2|3|4] Higher values will increase the radius of the effect.

uniforms.name: ClarityOffset
uniforms.label: ClarityOffset
uniforms.tip: Additional adjustment for the blur radius. Increasing the value will increase the radius.

uniforms.name: ClarityBlendMode
uniforms.label: ClarityBlendMode
uniforms.tip: Blend modes determine how the clarity mask is applied to the original image

uniforms.name: ClarityBlendIfDark
uniforms.label: ClarityBlendIfDark
uniforms.tip: Any pixels below this value will be excluded from the effect. Set to 50 to target mid-tones.

uniforms.name: ClarityBlendIfLight
uniforms.label: ClarityBlendIfLight
uniforms.tip: Any pixels above this value will be excluded from the effect. Set to 205 to target mid-tones.

uniforms.name: ClarityViewBlendIfMask
uniforms.label: ClarityViewBlendIfMask
uniforms.tip: The mask used for BlendIf settings. The effect will not be applied to areas covered in black

uniforms.name: ClarityStrength
uniforms.label: ClarityStrength
uniforms.tip: Adjusts the strength of the effect

uniforms.name: ClarityDarkIntensity
uniforms.label: ClarityDarkIntensity
uniforms.tip: Adjusts the strength of dark halos.

uniforms.name: ClarityLightIntensity
uniforms.label: ClarityLightIntensity
uniforms.tip: Adjusts the strength of light halos.

uniforms.name: ClarityViewMask
uniforms.label: ClarityViewMask
uniforms.tip: The mask is what creates the effect. View it when making adjustments to get a better idea of how your changes will affect the image.

uniforms.name: ColorMatrix_Red
uniforms.label: Matrix Red
uniforms.tip: How much of a red, green and blue tint the new red value should contain. Should sum to 1.0 if you don't wish to change the brightness.

uniforms.name: ColorMatrix_Green
uniforms.label: Matrix Green
uniforms.tip: How much of a red, green and blue tint the new green value should contain. Should sum to 1.0 if you don't wish to change the brightness.

uniforms.name: ColorMatrix_Blue
uniforms.label: Matrix Blue
uniforms.tip: How much of a red, green and blue tint the new blue value should contain. Should sum to 1.0 if you don't wish to change the brightness.

uniforms.name: Strength
uniforms.label: Strength
uniforms.tip: Adjust the strength of the effect.

techs.name: Capture
techs.label: Capture
techs.tip: Step 1: Capture original image before any effects.

techs.name: Restore
techs.label: Restore
techs.tip: Step 2: Capture Effect A and restore original image.

techs.name: Compare
techs.label: Compare
techs.tip: Step 3: Compare Effect A and Effect B with various visualization modes.

uniforms.name: Mode
uniforms.label: Mode
uniforms.tip: Choose what to apply contrast to.

uniforms.name: Formula
uniforms.label: Formula
uniforms.tip: The contrast s-curve you want to use. Note that Technicolor Cinestyle is practically identical to Sine, but runs slower. In fact I think the difference might only be due to rounding errors. I prefer 2 myself, but 3 is a nice alternative with a little more effect (but harsher on the highlight and shadows) and it's the fastest formula.

uniforms.name: Contrast
uniforms.label: Contrast
uniforms.tip: The amount of contrast you want.

uniforms.name: Short_Edge_Mask
uniforms.label: Short Edge AA
uniforms.tip:
Use this to adjust the Short Edge AA.
Default is 0.5

uniforms.name: Long_Edge_Mask
uniforms.label: Long Edge AA
uniforms.tip:
Use this to adjust the Long Edge AA.
Default is 0.5

uniforms.name: Text_Preservation
uniforms.label: Text Preservation
uniforms.tip:
Use this to adjust Text Preservation Power.
Default is 0.5

uniforms.name: Black_Preservation
uniforms.label: Black Preservation
uniforms.tip:
Use this to prevent Black Shades from getting AA Since most times this is not needed.
Default is 0.25

uniforms.name: View_Mode
uniforms.label: View Mode
items: Red H & Green V Short Edge Mask
Red H & Green V Long Edge Mask
uniforms.tip: This is used to select the normal view output or debug view.

uniforms.name: Strength
uniforms.label: Strength
uniforms.tip: Adjust the strength of the effect.

techs.name: Deband
techs.label: Deband
techs.tip: Alleviates color banding by trying to approximate original color values.

uniforms.name: enable_weber
uniforms.label: Weber ratio
uniforms.tip: Weber ratio analysis that calculates the ratio of the each local pixel's intensity to average background intensity of all the local pixels.

uniforms.name: enable_sdeviation
uniforms.label: Standard deviation
uniforms.tip: Modified standard deviation analysis that calculates nearby pixels' intensity deviation from the current pixel instead of the mean.

uniforms.name: enable_depthbuffer
uniforms.label: Depth detection
uniforms.tip: Allows depth information to be used when analysing banding, pixels will only be analysed if they are in a certain depth. (e.g. debanding only the sky)

uniforms.name: t1
uniforms.label: Standard deviation threshold
uniforms.tip: Standard deviations lower than this threshold will be flagged as flat regions with potential banding.

uniforms.name: t2
uniforms.label: Weber ratio threshold
uniforms.tip: Weber ratios lower than this threshold will be flagged as flat regions with potential banding.

uniforms.name: banding_depth
uniforms.label: Banding depth
uniforms.tip: Pixels under this depth threshold will not be processed and returned as they are.

uniforms.name: range
uniforms.label: Radius
uniforms.tip: The radius increases linearly for each iteration. A higher radius will find more gradients, but a lower radius will smooth more aggressively.

uniforms.name: iterations
uniforms.label: Iterations
uniforms.tip: The number of debanding steps to perform per sample. Each step reduces a bit more banding, but takes time to compute.

uniforms.name: debug_output
uniforms.label: Debug view
uniforms.tip:
Blurred (LPF) image: Useful when tweaking radius and iterations to make sure all banding regions are blurred enough.
Banding map: Useful when tweaking analysis parameters, continuous green regions indicate flat (i.e. banding) regions.

techs.name: DepthDarkness
techs.label: DepthDarkness
techs.tip:
Depth Darkness v1.0
===========================================

Super-simple shader to apply a darkness at a depth
with a softness edge

By Frans 'Otis_Inf' Bouma and is part of OtisFX
https://fransbouma.com | https://github.com/FransBouma/OtisFX

uniforms.name: FocusPlane
uniforms.label: Focus plane
uniforms.tip: The depth of the plane where the blur starts, related to the camera

uniforms.name: FocusRange
uniforms.label: Focus range
uniforms.tip:
The range around the focus plane that's more or less not blurred.
1.0 is the FocusPlaneMaxRange.

uniforms.name: FocusPlaneMaxRange
uniforms.label: Focus plane max range
uniforms.tip:
The max range Focus Plane for when Focus Plane is 1.0.
1000 is the horizon.

uniforms.name: BlendFactor
uniforms.label: Blend factor
uniforms.tip: How strong the effect is applied to the original image. 1.0 is 100%, 0.0 is 0%.

uniforms.name: EffectStrength
uniforms.label: EffectStrength
uniforms.tip: The strength of the effect. Range from 0.0, which means no effect, till 1.0 which means pixels are 100% blurred based on depth.

uniforms.name: FogColor
uniforms.label: FogColor
uniforms.tip: Color of the fog, in (red , green, blue)

uniforms.name: FogStart
uniforms.label: FogStart
uniforms.tip: Start of the fog. 0.0 is at the camera, 1.0 is at the horizon, 0.5 is halfway towards the horizon. Before this point no fog will appear.

uniforms.name: FogFactor
uniforms.label: FogFactor
uniforms.tip: The amount of fog added to the scene. 0.0 is no fog, 1.0 is the strongest fog possible.

uniforms.name: Depth_Map_Adjust
uniforms.label: Depth Map Adjustment
uniforms.tip: Adjust the depth map and sharpness distance.

uniforms.name: Depth_Map_Flip
uniforms.label: Depth Map Flip
uniforms.tip: Flip the depth map if it is upside down.

uniforms.name: DEPTH_DEBUG
uniforms.label: View Depth
uniforms.tip: Shows depth, you want close objects to be black and far objects to be white for things to work properly.

uniforms.name: No_Depth_Map
uniforms.label: No Depth Map
uniforms.tip: If you have No Depth Buffer turn this On.

uniforms.name: Shade_Power
uniforms.label: Shade Power
uniforms.tip:
Adjust the Shade Power This improves AO, Shadows, & Darker Areas in game.
Number 0.5 is default.

uniforms.name: Blur_Cues
uniforms.label: Blur Shade
uniforms.tip:
Adjust the to make Shade Softer in the Image.
Number 0.5 is default.

uniforms.name: Spread
uniforms.label: Shade Fill
uniforms.tip:
Adjust This to have the shade effect to fill in areas gives fakeAO effect.
This is used for gap filling.
Number 10.0 is default.

uniforms.name: Debug_View
uniforms.label: Depth Cues Debug
uniforms.tip: Depth Cues Debug output the shadeded output.

techs.name: DirectionalDepthBlur
techs.label: DirectionalDepthBlur
techs.tip:
Directional Depth Blur v1.5
===========================================

Directional Depth Blur is a shader for adding far plane directional blur
based on the depth of each pixel

Directional Depth Blur was written by Frans 'Otis_Inf' Bouma and is part of OtisFX
https://fransbouma.com | https://github.com/FransBouma/OtisFX

uniforms.name: FocusPlane
uniforms.label: Focus plane
uniforms.tip: The depth of the plane where the blur starts, related to the camera

uniforms.name: FocusRange
uniforms.label: Focus range
uniforms.tip:
The range around the focus plane that's more or less not blurred.
1.0 is the FocusPlaneMaxRange.

uniforms.name: FocusPlaneMaxRange
uniforms.label: Focus plane max range
uniforms.tip:
The max range Focus Plane for when Focus Plane is 1.0.
1000 is the horizon.

uniforms.name: BlurAngle
uniforms.label: Blur angle
uniforms.tip: The angle of the blur direction

uniforms.name: BlurLength
uniforms.label: Blur length
uniforms.tip: The length of the blur strokes per pixel. 1.0 is the entire screen.

uniforms.name: BlurQuality
uniforms.label: Blur quality
uniforms.tip:
The quality of the blur. 1.0 means all pixels in the blur length are
read, 0.5 means half of them are read.

uniforms.name: ScaleFactor
uniforms.label: Scale factor
uniforms.tip:
The scale factor for the pixels to blur. Lower values downscale the
source frame and will result in wider blur strokes.

uniforms.name: BlurType
uniforms.label: The blur type
uniforms.tip:
The blur type. Focus Point Targeting Strokes means the blur directions
per pixel are towards the Focus Point.

uniforms.name: FocusPoint
uniforms.label: Blur focus point
uniforms.tip:
The X and Y coordinates of the blur focus point, which is used for
the Blur type 'Focus Point Targeting Strokes'. 0,0 is the
upper left corner, and 0.5, 0.5 is at the center of the screen.

uniforms.name: FocusPointBlendColor
uniforms.label: Color
uniforms.tip:
The color of the focus point in Point focused mode. The closer a
pixel is to the focus point, the more it will become this color.
In (red , green, blue)

uniforms.name: FocusPointBlendFactor
uniforms.label: Color blend factor
uniforms.tip: The factor with which the focus point color is blended with the final image

uniforms.name: FocusPointViewFilterCircleOnMouseDown
uniforms.label: Show filter circle on mouse down
uniforms.tip:
For Focus Point Targeting Strokes blur type:
If checked, an overlay is shown with the current filter circle.
White means blur will be present,
transparent means no blur will be present

uniforms.name: FocusPointFadeBlurInFeatherBand
uniforms.label: Fade blur in feather band
uniforms.tip:
For Focus Point Targeting Strokes blur type:
If checked, it'll fade out the blur in the feather area in the filter circle

uniforms.name: FlipFadeBlurInFeatherBand
uniforms.label: Flip feather band
uniforms.tip:
For Focus Point Targeting Strokes blur type:
If checked, it'll flip the feather band from being towards the center to towards the edges

uniforms.name: FlipFocusPointTargetingBlurDirection
uniforms.label: Flip Focus Point Targeting strokes blur direction
uniforms.tip:
For Focus Point Targeting Strokes blur type:
If checked, it'll flip the direction of the blur from inside-to-outside to outside-to-inside

uniforms.name: FilterCircleRadius
uniforms.label: Filter circle radius
uniforms.tip:
For Focus Point Targeting Strokes blur type:
The radius of the filter circle.
All points within this circle are not or only partially blurred

uniforms.name: FilterCircleDeformFactors
uniforms.label: Filter circle deform factors
uniforms.tip:
For Focus Point Targeting Strokes blur type:
The radius factors for width and height of the filter circle.
1.0 means no deformation, another value means deformation in that direction

uniforms.name: FilterCircleRotationFactor
uniforms.label: Filter circle rotation factor
uniforms.tip:
For Focus Point Targeting Strokes blur type:
The rotation factor of the filter circle

uniforms.name: FilterCircleFeather
uniforms.label: Filter circle feather
uniforms.tip:
For Focus Point Targeting Strokes blur type:
The feather area within the filter circle.
1.0 means the whole inner area is feathered,
0.0 means no feather area.

uniforms.name: HighlightGain
uniforms.label: Highlight gain
uniforms.tip:
The gain for highlights in the strokes plane. The higher the more a highlight gets
brighter.

uniforms.name: BlendFactor
uniforms.label: Blend factor
uniforms.tip: How strong the effect is applied to the original image. 1.0 is 100%, 0.0 is 0%.

techs.name: DisplayDepth
techs.label: DisplayDepth
techs.tip:
This shader helps you set the right preprocessor settings for depth input.
To set the settings click on 'Edit global preprocessor definitions' and set them there - not in this shader.
The settings will then take effect for all shaders, including this one.

By default calculated normals and depth are shown side by side.
Normals (on the left) should look smooth and the ground should be greenish when looking at the horizon.
Depth (on the right) should show close objects as dark and use gradually brighter shades the further away objects are.

uniforms.name: fUIScale

RESHADE_DEPTH_INPUT_Y_SCALE=<right value>

If you know the right resolution of the games depth buffer then this scale value is simply the ratio
between the correct resolution and the resolution Reshade thinks it is.
For example:
If it thinks the resolution is 1920 x 1080, but it's really 1280 x 720 then the right scale is (1.5 , 1.5)
because 1920 / 1280 is 1.5 and 1080 / 720 is also 1.5, so 1.5 is the right scale for both the x and the y

Automatically adjust Blackpoint, Whitepoint, and remove color tints/casts while enhancing contrast.
Both correcting per individual channel, as well as Light/Dark colors are supported.
This shader will not adjust tinting applied in gamma, and this is considered out of scope.

Bloom

Bloom is an effect that causes diffraction of light around bright reflective or emittive sources

Preprocessor Settings

BLOOM_ENABLE_CA: Enables a chromatic aberration effect on bloom

BLOOM_QUALITY_0_TO_2: Sets the quality, 0 is full (and heavy!), 2 is low and very fast,
1 is high quality and best trade off between quality and performance

BLOOM_LOOPCOUNT: Limit to the amount of loops of the Width effect. Wider blooms may need higher
values (eg. max width is 300, this value should be 300)

BLOOM_LIMITER: Limiter to the bloom. Wider blooms may need lower values or the bloom starts to look
rectangular (eg. 0.0001 (default) is good to about width 100, after that start to decrease this value)

BLOOM_USE_FOCUS_BLOOM: Enables another pass to add a narrow bloom on top of the wide bloom

One can run effects on this LUT using Reshade and export the results in a PNG
screenshot. You can take this screenshot into your favorite image editor and
make it into a 4096x64 LUT texture that can be read by Reshade's LUT shaders.
This way you can safe performance by using a texture to apply your favorite
effects instead of Reshade's color manipulation shaders.

uniforms.name: hueMid
uniforms.label: Hue Selection (Middle)
uniforms.tip: 0 = Red, 0.167 = Yellow, 0.333 = Green, 0.5 = Cyan, 0.666 = Blue, 0.833 = Magenta

Enable depth based adjustments.
Make sure you have setup your depth buffer correctly.

techs.name: prod80_04_Magical_Rectangle
techs.label: prod80_04_Magical_Rectangle
techs.tip:
The Magical Rectangle

This shader gives you a rectangular shape on your screen that you can manipulate in 3D space.
It can blend on depth, blur edges, change color, change blending, change shape, and so on.
It will allow you to manipulate parts of the scene in various ways. Not withstanding; add mist,
remove mist, change clouds, create backgrounds, draw flares, add contrasts, change hues, etc. in ways
another shader will not be able to do.

This shader requires access to depth buffer for full functionality!

uniforms.name: Cyan2strip
uniforms.label: Cyan Dye Color

uniforms.tip: 3rd Layer for Fun, lower values increase contrast

uniforms.name: Saturation2

Width: Enable depth based adjustments.

Luma Fading Effects

uniforms.name: Enable_Diffusion
uniforms.label: Enable the lens diffusion effect
uniforms.tip: Enable a light diffusion that emulates the glare of a camera lens.

uniforms.name: Enable_Bleach_Bypass
uniforms.label: Enable the 'Bleach Bypass' effect
uniforms.tip: Enable a cinematic contrast effect that emulates a bleach bypass on film. Used a lot in war movies and gives the image a grittier feel.

uniforms.name: Enable_Static_Dither
uniforms.label: Apply static dither
uniforms.tip: Dither the diffusion. Only applies a static dither image texture.

uniforms.name: Enable_Dither
uniforms.label: Dither the final output
uniforms.tip: Dither the final result of the shader.

uniforms.name: Blend_Amount
uniforms.label: Blend Amount
uniforms.tip: Blend the effect with the original image.

uniforms.name: Bleach_Bypass_Amount
uniforms.label: Bleach Bypass Amount
uniforms.tip: Adjust the amount of the third diffusion layer.

uniforms.name: Diffusion_1_Amount
uniforms.label: Amount
uniforms.tip: Adjust the amount of the first diffusion layer.

uniforms.name: Diffusion_1_Radius
uniforms.label: Radius
uniforms.tip: Set the radius of the first diffusion layer.

uniforms.name: Diffusion_1_Gamma
uniforms.label: Gamma
uniforms.tip: Apply Gamma to first diffusion layer.

uniforms.name: Diffusion_1_Quality
uniforms.label: Sampling quality
uniforms.tip: Set the quality of the first diffusion layer. Number is the divider of how many times the texture size is divided in half. Lower number = higher quality, but more processing needed. (No need to adjust this.)

uniforms.name: Diffusion_2_Amount
uniforms.label: Amount
uniforms.tip: Adjust the amount of the second diffusion layer.

uniforms.name: Diffusion_2_Radius
uniforms.label: Radius
uniforms.tip: Set the radius of the second diffusion layer.

uniforms.name: Diffusion_2_Gamma
uniforms.label: Gamma
uniforms.tip: Apply Gamma to second diffusion layer.

uniforms.name: Diffusion_2_Quality
uniforms.label: Sampling quality
uniforms.tip: Set the quality of the second diffusion layer. Number is the divider of how many times the texture size is divided in half. Lower number = higher quality, but more processing needed. (No need to adjust this.)

uniforms.name: Diffusion_3_Amount
uniforms.label: Amount
uniforms.tip: Adjust the amount of the third diffusion layer.

uniforms.name: Diffusion_3_Radius
uniforms.label: Radius
uniforms.tip: Set the radius of the third diffusion layer.

uniforms.name: Diffusion_3_Gamma
uniforms.label: Gamma
uniforms.tip: Apply Gamma to third diffusion layer.

uniforms.name: Diffusion_3_Quality
uniforms.label: Sampling quality
uniforms.tip: Set the quality of the third diffusion layer. Number is the divider of how many times the texture size is divided in half. Lower number = higher quality, but more processing needed. (No need to adjust this.)

uniforms.name: OutlineColor
uniforms.label: Outline colour
uniforms.tip: The colour of the line. Any colour works; white reads as a rim of light and black as ink.

uniforms.name: BlendMode
uniforms.label: Blend
uniforms.tip: Replace paints the colour over the scene. Add brightens it, which gives a rim of light. Multiply darkens it, which gives ink.

uniforms.name: Thickness
uniforms.label: Thickness
uniforms.tip: Line width as a share of the screen's height, so it stays the same size whatever resolution the chain runs at.

uniforms.name: Sensitivity
uniforms.label: Sensitivity
uniforms.tip: How small a step in depth draws a line. Higher finds fainter edges, and at the very top starts to draw lines across flat ground.

uniforms.name: Softness
uniforms.label: Softness
uniforms.tip: Fades a line in over a range instead of cutting it hard.

uniforms.name: FadeStart
uniforms.label: Fade start
uniforms.tip: Distance in studs where lines start to fade. Assumes Roblox's near plane of 0.1 studs.

uniforms.name: FadeEnd
uniforms.label: Fade end
uniforms.tip: Distance in studs where lines are gone.

uniforms.name: Rotation
uniforms.label: Rotation
uniforms.tip: Turns the panorama around the vertical, in degrees, to put the sun or a cloud where you want it.

uniforms.name: HorizonShift
uniforms.label: Horizon height
uniforms.tip: Raises or lowers the panorama's horizon, in degrees, so it meets the game's own horizon instead of floating above or sinking below it.

uniforms.name: Exposure
uniforms.label: Exposure
uniforms.tip: Brightness in stops. Each step up doubles the light.

uniforms.name: Tint
uniforms.label: Tint
uniforms.tip: Multiplies the panorama's colour. White leaves it as it is.

uniforms.name: Contrast
uniforms.label: Contrast
uniforms.tip: Panoramas made from HDR photographs are often flat; this pulls the clouds out of the haze.

uniforms.name: Opacity
uniforms.label: Opacity
uniforms.tip: How much of the game's own sky is replaced. Lower lets it show through.

uniforms.name: EdgeBlend
uniforms.label: Edge blend
uniforms.tip: Paints a little of the new sky into the pixels at the edge of a building or a tree, which otherwise keep a thin line of the old sky's colour.

uniforms.name: Debug
uniforms.label: Show
uniforms.tip: Sky mask draws the replaced pixels in white, and red when the game's camera is not known. Panorama everywhere ignores depth, which shows the sky following the camera.

techs.name: PCGI_One
techs.label: RadiantGI
techs.tip: RadiantGI: Point Cloud Global Illumination.

uniforms.name: samples
uniforms.label: Samples
uniforms.tip: GI Sample Quantity is used to increase samples amount as a side effect this reduces noise.

uniforms.name: GI_Ray_Length
uniforms.label: General Ray Length
uniforms.tip:
General GI Ray Length is used to increase the Sampling Radius.
The byproduc of this causes the ray casting distance to extend.
This scales automatically with multi level detail.

uniforms.name: Target_Lighting
uniforms.label: Targeted Lighting
uniforms.tip:
Lets you target the Direct Lighting and/or Indirect Lighting specifically, so the shader can use your adjustment for its own GI calculations.
Negative values target Indirect lighting and positive values target direct lighting in the image./nDefaults is [0.05] and Zero is full image sampling.

uniforms.name: NCD
uniforms.label: Near Details
uniforms.tip:
Lets you adjust detail of objects near the cam and or like weapon hand GI.
The 2nd Option is for Weapon Hands in game that fall out of range.
Defaults are [Near Details X 0.125] [Weapon Hand Y 0.0]

uniforms.name: PCGI_Fade
uniforms.label: Depth Fade-Out
uniforms.tip:
GI Application Power that is based on Depth scaling for controlled fade In-N-Out.
Can be set from 0 to 1 and is Set to Zero for No Culling.
Default is 0.0.

uniforms.name: Reflectivness
uniforms.label: Diffusion Amount
uniforms.tip:
This basicly adds control for how defused the lighting should look on the ground.
Default is [1.0 | 0.5]. One is Max Diffusion and the value is length.

uniforms.name: Scattering
uniforms.label: Subsurface Light Transport
uniforms.tip:
Enable The Subsurface Light Transport Function to create a Subsurface Scattering effect.
Default is Off.

uniforms.name: Wrap
uniforms.label: Upper Scattering
uniforms.tip:
Control the Light Wrap Form Factor to adjust the Subsurface Scattering effect.
Default is [0.5].

uniforms.name: Deep_Scattering
uniforms.label: Deep Scattering
uniforms.tip:
Control Thickness Estimation Form Factor to create a Deep Tissue Scattering effect.
Default is [0.1].

uniforms.name: Luma_Map
uniforms.label: Tissue Luma Map
uniforms.tip:
Controls the Luma Map that lets bright lights approximate deep penotration of the tissue.
Default is [0.5].

uniforms.name: Internals
uniforms.label: Internal Flesh Color
uniforms.tip:
Since I can't tell what the internal color of the Deep Tissue you need to set this your self for RGB.
Defaults are [R 0.25] [B 0.0] [G 0.0] [L 0.5].

uniforms.name: Diffusion_Saturation_Power
uniforms.label: Subsurface Blur & Flesh Saturation
uniforms.tip:
Diffusion Blur is used too softens the lighting and makes the person a little more realistic by mimicking this effect skin has on light.
Simulate light diffusion favor red blurring over other colors.
Default are [0.5] [0.5].

uniforms.name: SSS_Seek
uniforms.label: Skin Detect Distance
uniforms.tip:
Lets you control how far we need to search and seek with the human skin tone detection algorithm for SSLT.
The 2nd option only shows if you use the special LUT for custom and or more accurate skin tone detection.
You can get this LUT @ https://github.com/BlueSkyDefender/AstrayFX/wiki/Subsurface-Light-Transport
Default is [0.25].

uniforms.name: Sky_Emissive_Selection
uniforms.label: Directional Sky & Emissive Mode
uniforms.tip:
Use this to add Directional Sky and or Emissive Mode.

Directional Sky Color:
Allows for the use of Sky Color Contribution to effect the world directly.

Emissive Mode:
Make all bright objects''Emissive Objects,'' based on approximated information from the emitter.

Default is Off.

uniforms.name: Sky_Adustment
uniforms.label: Sky Color Averaging
uniforms.tip: This lets you Average the sky color so you can have general color.

uniforms.name: D_Irradiance
uniforms.label: Distance Irradiance
uniforms.tip:
Distance Irradiance Lets you control Irradiance that comes from the Refracted Light from distant ground.
Default is [0.0] and Zero is Off.

uniforms.name: PCGI_2DTexture_Detail
uniforms.label: Texture Details & Falloff
uniforms.tip:
Lets you add Texture Details to PCGI so you can have added 2D texture information applyed to the GI.
Turn this on by adjusting the first slider and then adjusting it's falloff with the second.
Defaults are [0.0,0.5] and Zero is Off

uniforms.name: Trim
uniforms.label: Trim
uniforms.tip:
Trim GI by limiting how far the GI is able to effect the objects around them.
Directional Sky Color is negatively impacted by this option.
Use this mostly for Emissive Mode.
Default is [0.0] and Zero is Off.

uniforms.name: Blend
uniforms.label: Blend Mode
uniforms.tip: Use this to change the look of GI when applied to the final image.

uniforms.name: GI_Power
uniforms.label: Power
uniforms.tip:
Main overall GI application power control.
Default is [Power 1.0].

uniforms.name: HDR_BP
uniforms.label: HDR Extraction Power
uniforms.tip:
Use This to adjust the HDR Power, You can override this value and set it to like 1.5 or something.
Dedault is [0.5] and Zero and is Off.

uniforms.name: Depth_Map
uniforms.label: Depth Map Selection
uniforms.tip:
Linearization for the zBuffer also known as Depth Map.
DM0 is Z-Normal and DM1 is Z-Reversed.

uniforms.name: Depth_Map_Adjust
uniforms.label: Depth Map Adjustment
uniforms.tip:
This allows for you to adjust the DM precision.
Adjust this to keep it as low as possible.
Default is 7.5

uniforms.name: Offset
uniforms.label: Depth Map Offset
uniforms.tip:
Depth Map Offset is for non conforming ZBuffer.
It is rare that you would need to use this option.
Use this to make adjustments to DM 0 or DM 1.
Default and starts at Zero and it is Off.

uniforms.name: Depth_Map_Flip
uniforms.label: Depth Map Flip
uniforms.tip: Flip the depth map if it is upside down.

uniforms.name: SamplesXY
uniforms.label: Denoise Power
uniforms.tip:
This raises or lowers Samples used for the Final DeNoisers which in turn affects Performance.
This also has the side effect of smoothing out the image so you get that Normal Like Smoothing.
Default is 7 and you can override this a bit.

uniforms.name: GI_Res
uniforms.label: Resolution
uniforms.tip:
GI Resolution is used too increase performance at the cost of quality.
Larger adjustments from default will reduce noise and vice versa.
Default is automaticly adjusted based on current resolution.

uniforms.name: IGN_Toggle
uniforms.label: Interleaved Gradient Noise
uniforms.tip: In the on position it uses Interleaved Gradient Noise in stead of Regular Noise.

uniforms.name: Strength
uniforms.label: Strength
uniforms.tip: Adjust the strength of the effect.

techs.name: Smart_Sharp
techs.label: Smart_Sharp
techs.tip:
Suggestion : You Can Enable 'Performance Mode Checkbox,' in the lower bottom right of the ReShade's Main UI.
             Do this once you set your Smart Sharp settings of course.

uniforms.name: Depth_Map_Adjust
uniforms.label: Depth Map Adjustment
uniforms.tip: Adjust the depth map and sharpness distance.

uniforms.name: Depth_Map_Flip
uniforms.label: Depth Map Flip
uniforms.tip: Flip the depth map if it is upside down.

uniforms.name: No_Depth_Map
uniforms.label: No Depth Map
uniforms.tip: If you have No Depth Buffer turn this On.

uniforms.name: Sharpness
uniforms.label: Sharpening Strength
uniforms.tip:
Scaled by adjusting this slider from Zero to One to increase sharpness of the image.
Zero = No Sharpening, to One = Full Sharpening, and Past One = Extra Crispy.
Number 0.625 is Equal to AMD FidelityFX Contrast Adaptive Sharpening at max settings.
Number 0.625 is default.

uniforms.name: B_Grounding
uniforms.label: Coarseness
uniforms.tip:
Like Coffee pick how rough do you want this shader to be, really just adjusts the radius of the filter.
Fine -> Medium -> Coarse too what ever you think looks good.
Let me have fun with names and tooltips........
Number 0.0 is default.

uniforms.name: CAM_IOB
uniforms.label: CAM Ignore Overbright
uniforms.tip:
Instead of of allowing Overbright in the mask this allows sharpening of this area.
I think it's more accurate to leave this on.

uniforms.name: CA_Mask_Boost
uniforms.label: CAM Boost
uniforms.tip: This boosts the power of Contrast Adaptive Masking part of the shader.

uniforms.name: CA_Removal
uniforms.label: CAM Removal
uniforms.tip:
This removes the extra Contrast Adaptive Masking part of the shader.
Keep in mind This filter already has a level of Contrast Masking.
This is for people who like the Raw look of Bilateral Sharpen.
Noise reduction from the Bilateral Filter applies automatically.

uniforms.name: Debug_View
uniforms.label: Debug View
uniforms.tip:
This is to DeBug Smart Sharp and lets you fine tune the shader.
Let me have fun with names and tooltips.......

uniforms.name: F_DeNoise
uniforms.label: Smart Denoiser Options
uniforms.tip:
This Denoiser can help with Noise in the image.
LvL One DeNoiser Works with Smart Sharp Only.
LvL Two DeNoiser Works with other shaders. But, it's a little stronger.
LvL Three DeNoiser N/A Future add on.

uniforms.name: Denoise_Power
uniforms.label: Denoise Power
uniforms.tip:
Increase the Sharpening strength of the DeNoiser.
Number Zero is default, Off.

uniforms.name: ClampSharp
uniforms.label: Clamp Sharpen
uniforms.tip: This Clamps the output of the Sharpen Shader.

uniforms.name: BG
uniforms.label: Best Guess Sensitivity
uniforms.tip:
Increases the sensitiviy of the Algo used for gussing where the user is looking at.
Default is 0.9625. But, any value around 0.5 - 1.0 can be used. Decreasing this makes it stronger.

uniforms.name: SSC
uniforms.label: Snow Scape Adjust
uniforms.tip:
Increase persistence of the frames this is really the Temporal Part.
Default is 0.625. But, a value around 0.625 is recommended.

uniforms.name: HMP
uniforms.label: Height Map Scaling
uniforms.tip:
Increases the Detail that it takes from the color information from the world.
Default is 0.5. But, any value around 0 - 2 can be used.

uniforms.name: Elevation
uniforms.label: Elevation
uniforms.tip:
Increase Parallax Occlusion Mapping Elevation.
Default is 10. But, a value around 1-25 is recommended.

uniforms.name: I_Ice
uniforms.label: Invert Snow
uniforms.tip: Use this so you can invert the Height Map.

uniforms.name: Depth_Map_Adjust
uniforms.label: Depth Map Adjustment
uniforms.tip: Adjust the depth map and sharpness distance.

uniforms.name: Strength
uniforms.label: Strength
uniforms.tip: Adjust the strength of the effect.

uniforms.name: ColorStrength
uniforms.label: ColorStrength
uniforms.tip: Higher means darker and more intense colors.

uniforms.name: Saturation
uniforms.label: Saturation
uniforms.tip: Additional saturation control since this effect tends to oversaturate the image.

uniforms.name: Strength
uniforms.label: Strength
uniforms.tip: Adjust the strength of the effect.

uniforms.name: Clamping_Adjust
uniforms.label: Clamping Adjust
uniforms.tip:
Adjust Clamping that effects Blur.
Default is Zero.

uniforms.name: Persistence
uniforms.label: User Adjust
uniforms.tip:
Increase persistence of the frames this is really the Temporal Part.
Default is 0.25. But, a value around 0.05 is recommended.

uniforms.name: Similarity
uniforms.label: Depth Similarity
uniforms.tip:
Extra Image clamping based on Depth Similarities between Past and Current Depth for DeGhosing TAA.
Works on Depth & Color Delta is Selected and Depth is working in the game.
Default is 0.25.

uniforms.name: Delta_Power
uniforms.label: Color & Depth Delta Power
uniforms.tip:
Extra Image clamping based on delta between Past and Current Depth Buffer.
Only works on Depth Delta is Selected and Depth is working in the game.
Default is 0.25.

uniforms.name: Depth_Map_Adjust
uniforms.label: Depth Map Adjustment
uniforms.tip: Adjust the depth map and sharpness distance.

uniforms.name: Depth_CutOff
uniforms.label: Depth CutOff point
uniforms.tip:
Use this too set a TAA Cutoff point based on depth.
Default is 0.0.

uniforms.name: Depth_Map_Flip
uniforms.label: Depth Map Flip
uniforms.tip: Flip the depth map if it is upside down.

uniforms.name: Gamma
uniforms.label: Gamma
uniforms.tip: Adjust midtones. 1.0 is neutral. This setting does exactly the same as the one in Lift Gamma Gain, only with less control.

uniforms.name: Bleach
uniforms.label: Bleach
uniforms.tip: Brightens the shadows and fades the colors

uniforms.name: Defog
uniforms.label: Defog
uniforms.tip: How much of the color tint to remove

uniforms.name: Persistence
uniforms.label: Persistence
uniforms.tip:
Increase persistence longer the trail or afterimage.
If pushed out the effect is alot like long exposure.
This can be used for light painting in games.
1000/1 is 1.0, so 1/2 is 0.5 and so forth.
Default is 0.25, 0 is infinity.

uniforms.name: TQ
uniforms.label: Trail Blur Quality
uniforms.tip:
Adjust Trail Blur Quality.
Default is Zero.

uniforms.name: PS2
uniforms.label: PS2 Style Echo
uniforms.tip:
This enables PS2 Style Echo in your game.
This disables Trail Quality.

techs.name: UIMask_Top
techs.label: UIMask_Top
techs.tip: Place this *above* the effects to be masked.

techs.name: UIMask_Bottom
techs.label: UIMask_Bottom
techs.tip:
Place this *below* the effects to be masked.
If you want to add a toggle key for the effect, set it to this one.

uniforms.name: fMask_Intensity
uniforms.label: Mask Intensity
uniforms.tip:
How much to mask effects from affecting the original image.

Default: 1.0

uniforms.name: bDisplayMask
uniforms.label: Display Mask
uniforms.tip:
Display the mask texture.
Useful for testing multiple channels or simply the mask itself.

Default: Off

uniforms.name: Vibrance
uniforms.label: Vibrance
uniforms.tip: Intelligently saturates (or desaturates if you use negative values) the pixels depending on their original saturation.

uniforms.name: VibranceRGBBalance
uniforms.label: RGB Balance
uniforms.tip:
A per channel multiplier to the Vibrance strength so you can give more boost to certain colors over others.
This is handy if you are colorblind and less sensitive to a specific color.
You can then boost that color more than the others.

uniforms.name: Ratio
uniforms.label: Ratio
uniforms.tip: Sets a width to height ratio. 1.00 (1/1) is perfectly round, while 1.60 (16/10) is 60 % wider than it's high.

uniforms.name: Radius
uniforms.label: Radius
uniforms.tip: lower values = stronger radial effect from center

uniforms.name: Amount
uniforms.label: Amount
uniforms.tip: Strength of black. -2.00 = Max Black, 1.00 = Max White.

uniforms.name: Slope
uniforms.label: Slope
uniforms.tip: How far away from the center the change should start to really grow strong (odd numbers cause a larger fps drop than even numbers).

uniforms.name: Center
uniforms.label: Center
uniforms.tip: Center of effect for 'Original' vignette type. 'New' and 'TV style' do not obey this setting.

techs.name: Bloom
techs.label: Bloom
techs.tip:
>> qUINT::Bloom <<

Bloom is a shader that produces a glow around bright
light sources and other emitters on screen.

Bloom is written by Marty McFly / Pascal Gilcher

uniforms.name: BLOOM_CURVE
uniforms.label: Bloom Curve
uniforms.tip: Higher values limit bloom to bright light sources only.

uniforms.name: BLOOM_SAT
uniforms.label: Bloom Saturation
uniforms.tip: Adjusts the color strength of the bloom effect

uniforms.name: BLOOM_LAYER_MULT_1
uniforms.label: Bloom Layer 1 Intensity
uniforms.tip: Intensity of this bloom layer. 1 is sharpest layer, 7 the most blurry.

uniforms.name: BLOOM_LAYER_MULT_2
uniforms.label: Bloom Layer 2 Intensity
uniforms.tip: Intensity of this bloom layer. 1 is sharpest layer, 7 the most blurry.

uniforms.name: BLOOM_LAYER_MULT_3
uniforms.label: Bloom Layer 3 Intensity
uniforms.tip: Intensity of this bloom layer. 1 is sharpest layer, 7 the most blurry.

uniforms.name: BLOOM_LAYER_MULT_4
uniforms.label: Bloom Layer 4 Intensity
uniforms.tip: Intensity of this bloom layer. 1 is sharpest layer, 7 the most blurry.

uniforms.name: BLOOM_LAYER_MULT_5
uniforms.label: Bloom Layer 5 Intensity
uniforms.tip: Intensity of this bloom layer. 1 is sharpest layer, 7 the most blurry.

uniforms.name: BLOOM_LAYER_MULT_6
uniforms.label: Bloom Layer 6 Intensity
uniforms.tip: Intensity of this bloom layer. 1 is sharpest layer, 7 the most blurry.

uniforms.name: BLOOM_LAYER_MULT_7
uniforms.label: Bloom Layer 7 Intensity
uniforms.tip: Intensity of this bloom layer. 1 is sharpest layer, 7 the most blurry.

uniforms.name: BLOOM_ADAPT_STRENGTH
uniforms.label: Bloom Scene Adaptation Sensitivity
uniforms.tip: Amount of adaptation applied, 0 means same exposure for all scenes, 1 means complete autoexposure.

uniforms.name: BLOOM_ADAPT_EXPOSURE
uniforms.label: Bloom Scene Exposure Bias
uniforms.tip:
qUINT bloom employs eye adaptation to tune bloom intensity for scene differences.
This parameter adjusts the final scene exposure.

uniforms.name: BLOOM_ADAPT_SPEED
uniforms.label: Bloom Scene Adaptation Speed
uniforms.tip:
Eye adaptation data is created by exponential moving average with last frame data.
This parameter controls the adjustment speed.
Higher parameters let the image adjust more quickly.

uniforms.name: BLOOM_TONEMAP_COMPRESSION
uniforms.label: Bloom Tonemap Compression
uniforms.tip: Lower values compress a larger color range.

techs.name: Debanding
techs.label: Debanding
techs.tip:
>> qUINT::Debanding <<

This is a simple debanding filter, which aims to hide color
quantization artifacts in games. 

qUINT Debanding is written by Marty McFly / Pascal Gilcher

uniforms.name: BIT_DEPTH
uniforms.label: Bit depth of data to be debanded

techs.name: ADOF
techs.label: ADOF
techs.tip:
>> qUINT::ADOF <<

ADOF is a bokeh depth of field shader.
It blurs the scene in front of and behind the focus plane
to simulate the behaviour of real lenses. A multitude of features
allows to simulate various types of bokeh blur that cameras produce.

ADOF is written by Marty McFly / Pascal Gilcher

uniforms.name: fADOF_AutofocusCenter
uniforms.label: Autofocus Center
uniforms.tip: X and Y coordinates of autofocus center. Axes start from upper left screen corner.

uniforms.name: fADOF_AutofocusRadius
uniforms.label: Autofocus sample radius
uniforms.tip: Radius of area contributing to focus calculation.

uniforms.name: fADOF_AutofocusSpeed
uniforms.label: Autofocus Adjustment Speed
uniforms.tip: Adjustment speed of autofocus on focus change

uniforms.name: fADOF_ManualfocusDepth
uniforms.label: Manual focus depth
uniforms.tip: Manually adjusted static focus depth, disable autofocus to use it.

uniforms.name: fADOF_RenderResolutionMult
uniforms.label: Size Scale
uniforms.tip: Resolution Scale of bokeh blur. 0.5 means 1/2 screen width and height.

uniforms.name: fADOF_ShapeRadius
uniforms.label: Bokeh Maximal Blur Size
uniforms.tip: Blur size of areas entirely out of focus.

uniforms.name: fADOF_SmootheningAmount
uniforms.label: Gaussian blur width
uniforms.tip: Width of gaussian blur after bokeh filter.

uniforms.name: iADOF_BokehMode
uniforms.label: Bokeh highlight type
uniforms.tip: Different methods to emphasize bokeh sprites

uniforms.name: iADOF_ShapeVertices
uniforms.label: Bokeh shape vertices
uniforms.tip: Vertices of bokeh kernel. 5 = pentagon, 6 = hexagon etc.

uniforms.name: fADOF_ShapeCurvatureAmount
uniforms.label: Bokeh shape roundness
uniforms.tip: Roundness of bokeh kernel. 1.0 = circle, 0.0 = polygon.

techs.name: Lightroom
techs.label: Lightroom
techs.tip:
>> qUINT::Lightroom <<

Lightroom is a color grading toolbox that offers a multitude
of features commonly found in color grading software.
You can do deep color modifications, adjust contrast and levels,
tweak color balance, view a histogram and bake the CC into a 3D LUT.

Lightroom is written by Marty McFly / Pascal Gilcher

uniforms.name: LIGHTROOM_ENABLE_LUT
uniforms.label: Enable LUT Overlay
uniforms.tip:
This displays a neutral LUT onscreen, all color adjustments of this shader and consecutive ones are applied to it.
Taking a screenshot and using the cropped LUT with the TuningPalette will reproduce all changes of this shader.
To make sure that all color changes of your current preset are saved, put Lightroom as early in the
technique chain as possible. Putting grain, sharpening, bloom etc after Lightroom.fx will break the LUT.

uniforms.name: LIGHTROOM_LUT_TILE_SIZE
uniforms.label: LUT tile size
uniforms.tip: This controls the XY size of tiles of the LUT (which is accuracy in red/green channel).

uniforms.name: LIGHTROOM_LUT_TILE_COUNT
uniforms.label: LUT tile count
uniforms.tip:
This controls the amount of tiles of the LUT (which is accuracy in blue channel).
Be aware that Tile Size XY * Tile Amount is the width of the LUT and if this value
is larger than your resolution width, the LUT won't fit on your screen.

uniforms.name: LIGHTROOM_LUT_SCROLL
uniforms.label: LUT scroll
uniforms.tip:
If your LUT size exceeds your screen width, set this to 0, take screenshot, set it to 1, take screenshot
etc until you  reach the end of your LUT and assemble the screenshots like a panorama.
If your LUT fits the screen size however, leave it at 0.

uniforms.name: LIGHTROOM_ENABLE_CURVE_DISPLAY
uniforms.label: Enable Luma Curve Display
uniforms.tip:
This enables a small overlay with a luma curve
so you can monitor changes made by exposure, levels etc.

uniforms.name: LIGHTROOM_ENABLE_CLIPPING_DISPLAY
uniforms.label: Enable Black/White Clipping Mask
uniforms.tip:
This shows where colors reach #000000 black or #ffffff white, helpful for adjusting levels properly.
NOTE: Any shader that operates after Lightroom in ReShade technique list can change final color levels afterwards
so either put Lightroom last in line or take this with a grain of salt.

uniforms.name: LIGHTROOM_GLOBAL_BLACK_LEVEL
uniforms.label: Global Black Level
uniforms.tip: Scales input HSL value. Everything darker than this is mapped to black.

uniforms.name: LIGHTROOM_ENABLE_VIGNETTE
uniforms.label: Enable Vignette Effect
uniforms.tip: This enables a vignette effect (corner darkening).

uniforms.name: LIGHTROOM_VIGNETTE_SHOW_RADII
uniforms.label: Show Vignette Inner and Outer radius
uniforms.tip:
This makes the inner and outer radius setting visible.
Vignette intensity builds up from green (no vignetting) to red (full vignetting).

uniforms.name: LIGHTROOM_VIGNETTE_RADIUS_INNER
uniforms.label: Inner Vignette Radius
uniforms.tip: Anything closer to the screen center than this is not affected by vignette.

uniforms.name: LIGHTROOM_VIGNETTE_RADIUS_OUTER
uniforms.label: Outer Vignette Radius
uniforms.tip: Anything farther from the screen center than this gets fully vignette'd.

uniforms.name: LIGHTROOM_VIGNETTE_WIDTH
uniforms.label: Vignette Width
uniforms.tip: Higher values stretch the vignette horizontally.

uniforms.name: LIGHTROOM_VIGNETTE_HEIGHT
uniforms.label: Vignette Height
uniforms.tip: Higher values stretch the vignette vertically.

uniforms.name: LIGHTROOM_VIGNETTE_CURVE
uniforms.label: Vignette Curve
uniforms.tip: Curve of gradient between inner and outer radius. 1.0 means linear.

uniforms.name: LIGHTROOM_VIGNETTE_BLEND_MODE
uniforms.label: Vignette Blend Mode
uniforms.tip: Select between different ways of applying vignette

techs.name: MXAO
techs.label: MXAO
techs.tip:
>> qUINT::MXAO <<

MXAO is a screen-space ambient occlusion shader.
It adds diffuse shading to object corners to give more depth
and detail to the scene. Check out the preprocessor options to
get access to more functionality.

Make sure to move MXAO to the very top of your shader list for
maximum compatibility with other shaders.

MXAO is written by Marty McFly / Pascal Gilcher

uniforms.name: MXAO_GLOBAL_SAMPLE_QUALITY_PRESET
uniforms.label: Sample Quality
uniforms.tip: Global quality control, main performance knob. Higher radii might require higher quality.

uniforms.name: MXAO_SAMPLE_RADIUS
uniforms.label: Sample Radius
uniforms.tip: Sample radius of MXAO, higher means more large-scale occlusion with less fine-scale details.

uniforms.name: MXAO_SAMPLE_NORMAL_BIAS
uniforms.label: Normal Bias
uniforms.tip: Occlusion Cone bias to reduce self-occlusion of surfaces that have a low angle to each other.

uniforms.name: MXAO_GLOBAL_RENDER_SCALE
uniforms.label: Render Size Scale
uniforms.tip:
Factor of MXAO resolution, lower values greatly reduce performance overhead but decrease quality.
1.0 = MXAO is computed in original resolution
0.5 = MXAO is computed in 1/2 width 1/2 height of original resolution
...

uniforms.name: MXAO_SSAO_AMOUNT
uniforms.label: Ambient Occlusion Amount
uniforms.tip: Intensity of AO effect. Can cause pitch black clipping if set too high.

uniforms.name: MXAO_BLEND_TYPE
uniforms.label: Blending Mode
uniforms.tip:
Different blending modes for merging AO/IL with original color.
Blending mode 0 matches formula of MXAO 2.0 and older.

uniforms.name: MXAO_FADE_DEPTH_START
uniforms.label: Fade Out Start
uniforms.tip: Distance where MXAO starts to fade out. 0.0 = camera, 1.0 = sky. Must be less than Fade Out End.

uniforms.name: MXAO_FADE_DEPTH_END
uniforms.label: Fade Out End
uniforms.tip: Distance where MXAO completely fades out. 0.0 = camera, 1.0 = sky. Must be greater than Fade Out Start.

techs.name: DELC_Sharpen
techs.label: DELC_Sharpen
techs.tip:
>> qUINT::DELCS <<

DELCS is an advanced sharpen filter made to enhance texture detail.
It offers a local contrast detection method and allows to suppress
oversharpening on depth edges to combat common sharpen artifacts.
get access to more functionality.

DELCS is best positioned after most shaders but before film grain or such.
DELCS is written by Marty McFly / Pascal Gilcher

techs.name: SSR
techs.label: SSR
techs.tip:
>> qUINT::SSR <<

SSR adds screen-space reflections to the scene. This shader is
intended to only be used in screenshots as it will add reflections
to _everything_ - ReShade limitation.

SSR is written by Marty McFly / Pascal Gilcher

uniforms.name: SSR_FIELD_OF_VIEW
uniforms.label: Vertical Field of View
uniforms.tip:
Vertical FoV, should match camera FoV but since ReShade's
depth linearization is not always precise, this value
might differ from the actual value. Just set to what looks best.

uniforms.name: SSR_FRESNEL_EXP
uniforms.label: Reflection Exponent
uniforms.tip:
qUINT uses Schlick's fresnel approximation.
This parameter represents the power of the angle falloff.
Higher values restrict reflections to very flat angles.
Original Schlick value: 5.
The Fresnel Coefficient is set to 0 to match most surfaces.

uniforms.name: SSR_FADE_DIST
uniforms.label: Fade Distance
uniforms.tip:
Distance where reflection is completely faded out.
1 means infinite distance.

uniforms.name: SSR_RAY_INC
uniforms.label: Ray Increment
uniforms.tip:
Rate of ray step size growth.
A parameter of 1.0 means same sized steps,
2.0 means the step size doubles each iteration.
Increase if not the entire scene is represented (e.g. sky missing) at the cost of precision.

uniforms.name: SSR_ACCEPT_RANGE
uniforms.label: Acceptance Range
uniforms.tip: Acceptable error for ray intersection. Larger values will cause more coherent but incorrect reflections.

uniforms.name: SSR_JITTER_AMOUNT
uniforms.label: Ray Jitter Amount
uniforms.tip:
Changes ray step size randomly per pixel to produce
a more coherent reflection at the cost of noise that needs to be filtered away.

uniforms.name: SSR_FILTER_SIZE
uniforms.label: Filter Kernel Size
uniforms.tip: Size of spatial filter, higher values create more blurry reflections at the cost of detail.

uniforms.name: SSR_RELIEF_AMOUNT
uniforms.label: Surface Relief Height
uniforms.tip: Strength of embossed texture relief. Higher values cause more bumpy surfaces.

uniforms.name: SSR_RELIEF_SCALE
uniforms.label: Surface Relief Scale
uniforms.tip: Scale of embossed texture relief, lower values cause more high frequency relief.
